newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close up on China talk, cash market.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close up on China talk, cash market.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed firmer on talk China was seeking soybeans and soymeal plus slow farmer selling of soybeans amid firm cash basis markets, traders said.
"They're up on China talk, but that's nothing new," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
Strong indications filtered through markets that China last week bought U.S. soybeans and soymeal, traders said. China also may still be seeking beans and meal this week.
"There are still China rumors of additional meal and bean business," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Soy also found support from domestic news.
Values were further underpinned by reports of lower soybean yields as the U.S. harvest progresses and by sparse farmer selling of the new crop, traders said.
Evidence the market remains oversold also underscored the advances, they said.
The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for the November closed at 30.018 points, near the oversold status at 30 but above the 20 level a point generally considered a very oversold market.
Soybeans closed 1-1/2 to three cents per bushel higher, with November up 1-3/4 at $7.38-1/4.
But gain in soybeans were capped by forecasts for good harvest weather in the U.S. Midwest amid active harvesting.
Position squaring was featured before the release at 0730 CDT Friday of USDA's October crop production and supply/demand reports, the traders said.
"We just drifted all day and looking for direction. I expect more evening up tomorrow ahead of Friday's report," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
An average of analysts' estimates placed the 1996 U.S. soybean crop at 2.287 billion bushels, up from USDA's forecast in September for 2.270 billion and above the 1995 production of 2.152 billion.
Key players in the soybean pit included Prudential Securities' purchase of three million bushels of November and Continental Grain sales of one million November, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 45,000, down from 48,128 Tuesday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Farmers Commodities Corp bought 800 November $7.25 puts at five to 5-1/4 cents, Continental Grain bought 500 November $7.50 calls at 5-1/4 to 5-3/4 cents and ADM Investor Services bought 500 November $7.75 calls at 1-3/8 to 1-1/2 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 20,000, down from 22,453 Tuesday.
